sources.entry: AIWatch - Open-source real-time status dashboard for 30 AI services (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Mistral, Groq, and more). AI-powered incident analysis via hybrid Gemma 4 + Claude Sonnet, early detection vs official status pages, reliability scoring, Discord/Slack webhooks. Stack: Cloudflare Workers + KV + Workers AI.

summary.name: AIWatch
summary.one_liner: AIWatch is a real-time status dashboard that monitors the health and latency of dozens of AI services such as Claude, ChatGPT/OpenAI, Gemini, and Cursor.
use_cases: Check whether Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini is down before debugging
Compare API latency across LLM providers
Get alerted to AI service incidents via Discord or Slack
Track recent incidents across coding agents and inference providers
Monitor reliability of AI APIs a team depends on
summary.what_it_does: The page shows a dashboard of 49 AI services grouped by category (LLM APIs, coding agents, voice, inference and infrastructure, observability, video, image, AI apps), with current operational, degraded, and down counts and an average uptime figure. It lists recent incidents with their service, status, and duration. It also ranks services by current response latency in milliseconds, from OpenRouter at 39ms to Deepgram at about 3.7 seconds. The listing describes additional features: AI-powered incident analysis using a hybrid of Gemma 4 and Claude Sonnet, early detection compared with official status pages, reliability scoring, and Discord/Slack webhooks. The stack is Cloudflare Workers, KV, and Workers AI.
notable: Covers 49 AI services with live status, incident feed, and latency rankings
AI-powered incident analysis combining Gemma 4 and Claude Sonnet
Early detection compared against official vendor status pages
Built on Cloudflare Workers, KV, and Workers AI
caveats: The page text does not state a license, so the open-source claim comes only from the listing.
Page text is mostly a dashboard snapshot; the listing's 30-service count differs from the 49 shown on the page.
